diffs.diff: temperature_C: datasheet reading gives 0.0625 per count, the part's model has none
diffs.evidence: DS1822 datasheet, OPERATION—MEASURING TEMPERATURE: "The resolution of the temperature sensor is user-configurable to 9, 10, 11, or 12 bits, corresponding to increments of 0.5°C, 0.25°C, 0.125°C, and 0.0625°C, respectively. The default resolution at power-up is 12 bit." and "The temperature data is stored as a 16-bit sign-extended two's complement number in the temperature register". The model already states the same scale: part.json description '0.0625 °C at the default 12 bits' and buildNotes 'Temperature = signed 16-bit register x 0.0625 °C'. The model uses sim kind 'onewire-temp', whose conversion is fixed in the simulator (src/sim/engine.ts owTemp: 'default 12-bit resolution: 0.0625 °C steps', Math.round(value*16)/16) instead of a measure/scale field, so the publish gate's extractor finds no scale constant; the scale itself is identical (0.0625 °C/LSB). The example uses MicroPython's ds18x20 driver, which applies this conversion for family 22h.
